clue.text: Language, by gum!

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise, 'by gum!', tacked onto talk about language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By gum!' reads as a mild Northern English oath, but here 'gum' is the second definition: gum arabic.
explanation.definitionFit: The tongue of the Middle East is one sense; the other is the acacia resin called gum arabic, used as glue.

clue.text: Watch salesman with consumer

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
an eater is one who consumes food

explanation.surface: A request to keep an eye on a salesman who comes with a customer.
explanation.definitionFit: A repeater is a pocket timepiece that chimes the hours when a lever is pressed.

clue.text: They give capital support in retirement

definitions.text: They give capital support in retirement

parts.words: They give capital support in retirement
parts.note: capital is read as the head, and retirement as going to bed: long pillows that prop the head at night

explanation.surface: Pension funds that keep money working for people who have stopped working.
explanation.definitionFit: Long firm pillows lie across a bed to raise the sleeper's head.

clue.text: Increasing noise in the bars

parts.note: bars are the measures of written music, not pubs, so this is a musical swell in volume

explanation.surface: Pubs getting louder as the evening wears on.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, a gradual build in loudness over several measures is marked with this Italian term.

clue.text: See me writing to a little Hibernian lady in India

parts.note: taken as written
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing
Hib is a short form of Hibernian, an Irish person

explanation.surface: An invitation to watch someone write a letter to a small Irish woman living in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is a link inviting the solver to look. 'Little' signals the shortened form of Hibernian.
explanation.definitionFit: Under the Raj, a European married woman in India was addressed by servants with this title.

clue.text: New Bolivia army tune assists troop movements

indicators.note: something new is freshly made, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A fresh Bolivian army march helps the soldiers keep step.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' looks like an extra N, but the fifteen letters of BOLIVIA ARMY TUNE already fill the answer, so 'New' must be the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The quality of being easily steered or redeployed is what lets an army shift its units quickly.

clue.text: Bond the explorer loses a ton

indicators.note: losing something means it is taken away, so these letters are removed from the explorer's name

parts.note: Ernest Shackleton was the famous Antarctic explorer
taken as written

explanation.surface: A secret agent called Bond, or an adventurer, sheds a lot of weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' suggests James Bond, but it is the definition: a fetter.
explanation.definitionFit: A fetter or restraint, such as a chain on a prisoner's wrist, is a binding tie.

clue.text: Why did the Suffolk punch? Because he saw' the

definitions.text: Why did the Suffolk punch? Because he saw' the

parts.words: Why did the Suffolk punch? Because he saw' the
parts.note: a Suffolk Punch is a breed of heavy horse; punching is boxing, so the horse threw punches on seeing a horse's travelling crate

explanation.surface: A riddle about why a farm horse lashed out.
explanation.walkthrough: A Suffolk Punch is an English breed of heavy draught horse. The answer split into two words gives a horse and boxing.
explanation.definitionFit: A trailer for carrying horses by road is a stall on wheels.

clue.text: Exiles Caliban; is he still hiding here?

indicators.note: the answer is concealed within the run of words before it, like someone hiding in that phrase

explanation.surface: Prospero sends Caliban away from the island and wonders whether the creature is still lurking about.
explanation.walkthrough: Caliban is the island creature in Shakespeare's The Tempest. 'Hiding here' points to the letters inside 'Caliban; is he still'.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive someone out of the country is to send them into exile.

clue.text: Pat, a young rascal …

parts.note: Pat is the stock name for an Irishman, so this is an Irish word for a rogue or good-for-nothing

explanation.surface: Introducing a boy named Pat as a little scamp.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on into the next clue. Pat is the stock name for an Irishman, pointing to an Irish word.
explanation.definitionFit: An Irish term for a worthless fellow or scamp, originally a migrant labourer.

clue.text: : meets another boy. 3 kind of saint

annotationWithheld.why: : meets another boy. 3 kind of saint: the scan reads '... : meets another boy, a kind of saint', running on from 9's 'Pat'; the PAT piece is in 9's clue, so this clue holds no word giving it
annotationWithheld.clue: : meets another boy. 3 kind of saint

clue.text: A song can take one's fancy heard in church

indicators.note: words heard in church are spoken or sung aloud, so the phrase is judged by its sound

parts.note: to tickle someone's fancy is to please them, so 'can take one's fancy' is 'can tickle'

explanation.surface: A hymn sung in church that appeals to the listener.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the song; 'heard in church' says the two words 'can tickle' are said aloud, and the church sets the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A hymn or chant whose words come from the Bible, sung in church services.

clue.text: Top sports people on the way down?

definitions.text: Top sports people on the way down?

parts.words: Top sports people on the way down?
parts.note: top sports people sound like champions in decline, but these are people who start at the top of a slope and descend

explanation.surface: Star athletes whose careers are fading.
explanation.definitionFit: People on skis descend a mountain from its summit.

clue.text: To make good, Tree put himself out about a new star

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters go round the star
putting oneself out of order, Tree's own letters are rearranged

parts.note: Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a famous actor-manager
a nova is a star that suddenly flares up, Latin for new

explanation.surface: The actor-manager Tree made an effort to repair matters for a new leading actor.
explanation.walkthrough: Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a celebrated Edwardian actor-manager; 'put himself out' scrambles his name into RETE, and 'about' sets that round the star.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore something to good condition is to refurbish or repair it.

clue.text: The alternative is clear, of course

definitions.text: The alternative is clear, of course

parts.words: The alternative is clear, of course
parts.note: on a menu the soup course is offered either clear or the other kind

explanation.surface: Someone saying the other option is obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: A menu offers the first course as consommé or as a heavy, dense broth.

clue.text: Like hidden lamps in old sepulchral —" (Cowper)

definitions.text: Like hidden lamps in old sepulchral —" (Cowper)

parts.words: Like hidden lamps in old sepulchral —" (Cowper)
parts.note: a line of William Cowper's verse with its last word missing: ancient burial vessels

explanation.surface: A line of poetry with its final word left blank.
explanation.walkthrough: The poet William Cowper wrote of lamps hidden in old burial vessels; fill the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: Vases for holding the ashes of the dead were placed in ancient tombs.

clue.text: The beginnings of their social climbing?

definitions.text: The beginnings of their social climbing?

parts.words: The beginnings of their social climbing?
parts.note: climbing begins by going up, so these people's starts are upward ones: new arrivals who push to rise in society

explanation.surface: How social climbers first got going.
explanation.definitionFit: People who have risen suddenly in rank and behave with arrogance are parvenus.

clue.text: A clean sweep with this

parts.note: the proverb says a new brush sweeps clean: a newcomer makes sweeping changes

explanation.surface: A promise of total victory, or a tidy floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A newly appointed person keen to make sweeping changes is named after an unused sweeping brush.

clue.text: Fascist" weapons in revolutionary centres

explanation.surface: Weapons used by Fascists in the heart of a revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: The fasces, the rods and axe carried before Roman magistrates, gave Fascism its name.
explanation.definitionFit: Chopping tools bound in the fasces, emblem of Fascism; also the lines round which things rotate.

clue.text: Sapling that didn't survive the fire?

definitions.text: Sapling that didn't survive the fire?

parts.words: Sapling that didn't survive the fire?
parts.note: a young tree reduced to cinders; really a young tree of a particular kind, cut as a walking stick

explanation.surface: A young tree lost in a blaze.
explanation.definitionFit: A walking stick cut from a young tree of the genus Fraxinus.

clue.text: A grounding in radio circuitry

parts.note: a grounding sounds like basic training, but here it is the electrical connection to the ground

explanation.surface: A basic course in radio electronics.
explanation.definitionFit: Connecting an electrical circuit to the ground for safety is the British term.

clue.text: With a worried air South kept a bridge engagement

definitions.text: With a worried air South kept a bridge engagement

parts.words: With a worried air South kept a bridge engagement
parts.note: South is a bridge card player, but the bridge kept here is the one over the Tiber held against an army

explanation.surface: A nervous bridge player in the South seat keeps a date for a game.
explanation.walkthrough: Horatius Cocles is the Roman hero who held the bridge over the Tiber, told in Macaulay's poem.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary Roman held the Sublician bridge alone against the Etruscan army.

clue.text: Encourage us to listen to X

parts.note: to hear is to listen to
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: A request that we pay attention to a mystery person.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheer up or embolden someone is to put heart into them.

clue.text: Raphael's protege given to prejudice

parts.note: taken as written
bias is a prejudice

explanation.surface: The painter Raphael's protégé had biased views.
explanation.walkthrough: Not the painter: in the Book of Tobit the archangel Raphael guides the young man on his journey. 'Given' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Apocrypha, the archangel guides and protects the son of Tobit on his travels.

clue.text: Skipton's worried by black marks

indicators.note: worried means shaken about, so the letters of the town's name are jumbled

explanation.surface: The Yorkshire town of Skipton is troubled by its bad reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: Skipton is a market town in North Yorkshire. Here its 's supplies a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Blots of dark fluid left by a pen on paper.

clue.text: Places for observing the layers of sleep? On the contrary'

definitions.text: Places for observing the layers of sleep? On the contrary'

parts.words: Places for observing the layers of sleep? On the contrary'
parts.note: reversed, the phrase reads places for sleep of the layers, layers being egg-laying hens

explanation.surface: A scientist wants somewhere to study the stages of sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' swaps the phrase round: places for the sleep of layers, i.e. laying hens.
explanation.definitionFit: Perches where hens and other birds settle for the night.

clue.text: Perhaps one cobra is causing such lines of depression?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: perhaps says the letters might be arranged another way, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A snake might be causing someone to feel down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' rearranges COBRA IS into SOBARIC after the I. The weather map's lines join points of equal pressure, and a depression is a low.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes lines on a weather map joining points of equal atmospheric pressure, as round a low.

clue.text: Hence three little maids

parts.note: Gilbert and Sullivan's Mikado has 'Three little maids from school', so this is where they came from

explanation.surface: Three girls who come from somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Three little maids from school are we' is a song in Gilbert and Sullivan's The Mikado; 'hence' means from here.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a school, especially a private academy for young ladies.

clue.text: For example, a top back 14

indicators.note: back says the whole string of pieces is read in reverse order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to put a lid back on, by way of illustration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' turns the whole run EG A TOP into POTAGE. The definition points to 14-down.
explanation.definitionFit: A French term for a dense, hearty soup.
